 Share Comments Stock Market Today Highlights: Sensex plunges over 400 points, Nifty50 tumbles below 22,700
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 22, 2026, 16:18:55 IST SUMMARY Dalal Street remained under pressure on Thursday as rising crude oil prices, renewed geopolitical tensions and weakness in the rupee dampened investor sentiment. The Sensex fell 460.30 points to settle at 73,249.39, while the Nifty slipped below the 22,700 mark, closing 123.70 points lower at 22,687.65. 
 Both benchmarks registered their third consecutive session of losses amid widespread selling across sectors. Global oil prices surged following reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure, with Brent crude rising over 3 per cent to $112.33 per barrel. 
 The rupee also weakened sharply, declining 44 paise to close at 94.82 against the US dollar. Media, FMCG and IT stocks faced selling pressure, while heavyweight stocks including Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank contributed to the market's decline. 
 Track TOI’s coverage on BSE Sensex and Nifty50 to know which way stock markets are headed: Live Events 
 16:16 (IST) Oct 22 Bajaj Finance, Cipla lead Nifty gainers; Nestle India, Eternal top losers Bajaj Finance emerged as the top Nifty gainer, rising 1.74 per cent, followed by Cipla (1.29 per cent), UltraTech Cement (1.00 per cent), ICICI Bank (0.97 per cent) and Bajaj Auto (0.82 per cent). On the losing side, Nestle India declined 2.78 per cent, followed by Eternal (2.53 per cent), HDFC Life (2.09 per cent), Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (2.07 per cent) and Reliance Industries (2.03 per cent). 16:15 (IST) Oct 22 Bajaj Finance, UltraTech Cement lead Sensex gainers; Reliance, Eternal top losers Bajaj Finance rose 1.61 per cent to emerge as the top Sensex gainer on Thursday, followed by UltraTech Cement, which advanced 1.52 per cent. ICICI Bank, Sun Pharma and SBI also closed higher. On the losing side, Reliance Industries fell 2.59 per cent, leading the declines, followed by Eternal (2.20 per cent), HDFC Bank (1.85 per cent), Power Grid (1.71 per cent) and Trent (1.56 per cent). 16:14 (IST) Oct 22 Sensex plunges over 400 points, Nifty slips below 22,700 amid rising crude prices, geopolitical tensions Indian equity benchmarks extended their losing streak to a third consecutive session on Thursday, with the Sensex falling 460 points and the Nifty slipping below 22,700. Persistent selling across sectors, led by media stocks, along with elevated crude oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty, weighed on sentiment. Both benchmark indices ended lower, while broader markets also closed in the red. 13:58 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Top gainers and losers on BSE Sensex UltraTech Cement was the top gainer among the stocks listed, rising 1.24% to Rs 10,945. Bajaj Finance followed, gaining 1.12% to Rs 935.50, while Bharti Airtel advanced 0.95% to Rs 1,910.30. Larsen & Toubro (L&T) climbed 0.77% to Rs 3,658.10, and ICICI Bank rose 0.56% to Rs 1,392.70. Kotak Mahindra Bank edged up 0.34% to Rs 438, while State Bank of India (SBI) gained 0.19% to Rs 965.75. Sun Pharma was marginally higher, up 0.01% at Rs 1,745.20. 
 On the losing side, Eternal was among the biggest decliners, falling 2.21% to Rs 304.85. Tech Mahindra dropped 2.11% to Rs 1,796.30, while Bharat Electronics (BEL) declined 1.91% to Rs 364.50. Power Grid Corporation fell 1.89% to Rs 247.15, and HDFC Bank slipped 1.83% to Rs 693.50. Trent shed 1.81% to Rs 2,767.90, followed by Infosys, which fell 1.73% to Rs 1,147.25. Titan declined 1.60% to Rs 4,310, while Reliance Industries lost 1.57% to Rs 1,188.30. ITC fell 1.47% to Rs 257.90, Hindustan Unilever dropped 1.39% to Rs 1,819.40, and Asian Paints declined 1.33% to Rs 2,293.20.
 13:29 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: BSE Sensex plunges over 550 points, Nifty50 slips below 22,700 mark The BSE Sensex was trading 569.09 points, or 0.77%, lower at 73,140.60, while the Nifty 50 declined 195.40 points, or 0.86%, to 22,615.95. 12:21 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: BSE Sensex tumbles over 600 points, Nifty50 slips to 22,600 Dalal Street tumbled once again in afternoon trade after recovering. BSE Sensex was trading 638.98 points, or 0.87%, lower at 73,070.71, while NSE Nifty50 fell 210 points, or 0.92%, to 22,601.35. Daily Puzzles

 10:27 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Rupee offsets gains as Dalal Street struggles
 Rupee weakened in early trade on Thursday, losing 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar as rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall. Read full story › 10:06 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: BSE Sensex slumps over 400 points; top gainers in early trend BSE Sensex remained under pressure in morning trade, falling 578.92 points, or 0.79%, to 73,130.77. Despite the benchmark’s decline, some stocks traded in positive territory. Bharti Airtel led the gainers, rising 0.75% to Rs 1,906.65, followed by Infosys, which gained 0.21% to Rs 1,169.80. Kotak Mahindra Bank advanced 0.19% to Rs 437.35, while Eternal edged up 0.14% to Rs 312.20. 09:37 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Large-caps gain favour as liquidity-driven mid- and small-cap rally faces pressure Dr V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, said the market was witnessing a shift towards large-cap stocks after a period of outperformance by mid- and small-cap shares. He said that the broader market’s resilience in recent months had been driven more by liquidity than by earnings growth. Vijayakumar noted that the gap between overvalued mid- and small-cap stocks, particularly small-caps, and attractively valued large-cap stocks was unlikely to persist for long. He also flagged elevated crude oil prices and high US bond yields as external risks that were fuelling bearish positions in the market. According to him, the shift towards fairly valued large-cap stocks is likely to continue. 09:27 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: NSE Nifty50 slips over 1% in opening trade Benchmarks extended their losses in early trade on Thursday, with NSE Nifty50 declining over 1%. BSE Sensex fell 610.57 points, or 0.83%, to 73,099.12, while Nifty 50 dropped 242.70 points, or 1.06%, to 22,568.65. 09:21 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: BSE Sensex tumbles over 500 points in opening trade Dalal Street opened sharply lower on Thursday, with Sensex tumbling over 500 points and Nifty50 slipping below the 22,700 mark. The BSE Sensex fell 546.45 points, or 0.74%, to 73,163.24, while NSE Nifty 50 declined 123.60 points, or 0.54%, to 22,687.75 in early trade. 08:39 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Gift Nifty signals weak start for domestic markets Gift Nifty was trading at 22,643.5, down 85 points or 0.37%, indicating a weak start for equity markets. The negative signal comes after benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty reversed early gains to close lower on Wednesday, extending their losses for a second consecutive session. Elevated crude oil prices, firm US bond yields and persistent macroeconomic concerns have weighed on investor sentiment. With oil prices rising again amid escalating tensions in the Gulf, market participants will be watching whether domestic equities face further selling pressure at the opening. 08:38 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Asian markets under pressure as Gulf tensions weigh on sentiment Asian equities struggled to sustain gains in early trade on Thursday as uncertainty surrounding the Gulf and concerns over artificial intelligence offset optimism around technology earnings. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.2%, putting it on track for a fourth consecutive weekly decline. Japan’s Nikkei gave up earlier gains to trade 0.4% lower, while South Korean shares fell more than 1%. In the broader regional market snapshot provided, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 2.09%, South Korea’s Kospi fell 1.92% and Shenzhen lost 1.41%. Shanghai was down 0.69%, while Australia’s ASX 200 slipped 0.47%. The mixed-to-negative regional cues come as investors assess geopolitical risks and their potential implications for oil prices and global market sentiment. 
 08:37 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market today: Oil prices climb as Houthi attacks raise Gulf supply concerns Oil prices rose on Thursday as fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the kingdom. Brent crude futures gained $1.29, or 1.2%, to $110.11 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 97 cents, or 1%, to $98.12. The latest escalation follows attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, including a strike at a civilian airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight, and a drone attack on an oil field that killed two people. Meanwhile, Iran’s foreign minister said the country was prepared to defend itself, while President Masoud Pezeshkian questioned the possibility of dialogue amid US pressure. The developments have added to uncertainty over regional security and energy supplies. 
 08:35 (IST) Oct 22 Rupee rallies 53 paise to six-week high Rupee strengthened 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by foreign currency inflows linked to Reliance Industries’ Jio Platforms IPO and intervention by the Reserve Bank of India. 
 The currency opened at 94.78, touched an intraday high of 94.35 and a low of 94.82 before settling at its strongest level in around six weeks. 
 However, weak domestic equities and elevated crude oil prices continued to pose risks to the currency’s gains. Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said the rupee could maintain a positive bias amid broad dollar weakness and softer US Treasury yields. The USD-INR spot rate is expected to trade in a range of Rs 94.20 to Rs 94.80, he said. 
 08:32 (IST) Oct 22 Stock market recap: Sensex, Nifty reverse early gains to end lower Benchmark indices closed lower on Wednesday for a second consecutive session as selling in power, banking and financial stocks offset early gains. BSE Sensex declined 143.21 points, or 0.19%, to settle at 73,709.69, despite rising as much as 829.29 points to an intraday high of 74,682.19 before noon. Profit booking dragged the index more than 1,450 points from its high to a low of 73,229.45, before some late buying helped it recover. NSE Nifty50 fell 77.60 points, or 0.34%, to close at 22,811.35, after moving between 23,120.90 and 22,702.85. Midcap and smallcap indices also declined around 1.5% to 2.4%, reflecting broader risk aversion, according to Ajit Mishra, SVP–Research at Religare Broking. 
 Indian equity markets extended their losing streak for the third consecutive session on Thursday, with the Sensex plunging 460.30 points, or 0.62 per cent, to close at 73,249.39, while the Nifty declined 123.70 points, or 0.54 per cent, to settle at 22,687.65. 
Elevated crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia weighed on investor sentiment, triggering broad-based selling across domestic markets. Most sectoral indices ended in the red, with media stocks emerging as the biggest laggards, falling over 2 per cent, followed by FMCG and IT stocks. Bajaj Finance, UltraTech Cement and ICICI Bank were among the notable gainers, while Reliance Industries, Eternal and HDFC Bank dragged the benchmarks lower. 
Meanwhile, Brent crude climbed above $112 per barrel, adding to concerns over inflation and India's import costs.
